summary: Lunar south pole missions face extreme lighting and communication constraints, yet existing tools like Quickmap and JPL Horizons are built for specialists and slow down rapid site evaluation. moonpie is an intuitive web application that lets mission planners, educators, and the public quickly compare lunar landing sites and dates. It renders a 3D Moon globe with a prominent landing site marker that users can click to open a detailed panel showing Sun and Earth positions relative to the horizon, solar elevation for power assessment, Earth visibility for communications, LOLA terrain variation, and nearby candidate sites. An off-screen indicator arrow always points to the selected site so it is never lost.
details:
moonpie is a web application for rapid lunar landing site evaluation, addressing the challenge that tools like NASA Quickmap, Moon Trek, and JPL Horizons are powerful but complex for non-specialists to use for quick site-date comparisons.

What it does:

  • Renders an interactive 3D Moon globe with a prominent landing site marker (pulsing glow halo, flag pole, radar ring) so the site is never hard to find
  • Lets users click directly on the landing site in the 3D view to open a detailed information panel
  • Accepts natural language queries via an AI mission assistant with quick action pills, conversational chat thread and instant scene updates, including slip-window scanning, landing area checks, and site scoring.
  • Shows Sun and Earth positions relative to the local horizon at the selected site, date, and time
  • Calculates solar elevation for power generation assessment and Earth visibility for direct-to-Earth communications
  • Displays LOLA terrain horizon profile charts and terrain variation stats (min/max elevation)
  • Renders a Moon map canvas with the landing site highlighted, a landing ellipse, and nearby candidate sites sorted by distance
  • Provides an off-screen indicator arrow that always points to the landing site, even when it's on the far side of the Moon
  • Supports date/time selection with diurnal playback to explore how lighting and communications change across a lunar day
  • Includes preset sites from Apollo, Luna, and CLPS targets (Shackleton, Malapert, Haworth) plus custom coordinate input

Intended impact: Bridges the gap between technical lunar data (ephemeris, LOLA topography) and an accessible interface for mission planners, educators, and the public to quickly evaluate whether a site-date combination is viable for power and communications.

Creativity: Rather than burying site info in a sidebar next to a share button, moonpie makes the landing site itself the interactive entry point, clicking the site on the Moon opens everything you need to know about it.
The AI assistant lets planners use plain language instead of navigating menus, making complex ephemeris and terrain data accessible through conversation.

Github: https://github.com/NASASpaceAppsITM2026
